title: Self-driving trucks begin testing on California highways under new DMV regulations
summary: Aurora Innovation and Kodiak AI have received permits from the California DMV to test self-driving trucks on public highways, marking a significant step in autonomous vehicle deployment. The updated regulations, effective April 2026, lifted a previous ban on heavy-duty autonomous vehicles over 10,000 pounds. Testing requires a human safety operator and excludes low-speed roads unless on a direct route. Both companies previously focused operations in Texas due to California's restrictions. The move has sparked legal opposition from labor groups over economic and safety concerns.
key_points: Aurora Innovation and Kodiak AI received California DMV permits to test self-driving trucks on public highways.
New DMV rules (April 2026) lifted a ban on heavy-duty autonomous vehicles (>10,000 lbs) in California.
Testing requires a human safety operator and restricts operations on roads with speed limits ≤25 mph unless on a direct route.
Both companies previously tested in Texas due to California’s prior restrictions; Kodiak has begun limited testing in Mountain View.
Aurora operates commercial routes in Texas (e.g., Dallas-Houston), while Kodiak expanded from off-road to on-highway operations in 2025.
Teamsters California filed a lawsuit alleging the DMV bypassed economic impact studies and safety risk assessments.
